title: Maximum Height by Stacking Cuboids
summary: Given n cuboids with dimensions cuboids[i] = [widthi, lengthi, heighti], select a subset and stack them.
statement: Given n cuboids with dimensions cuboids[i] = [widthi, lengthi, heighti], select a subset and stack them. Cuboid i can be placed on cuboid j if its width, length, and height are all less than or equal to those of cuboid j. Cuboids can be rotated to fit. Find the maximum height achievable by stacking.
constraints: There are 1 through 100 cuboids with three positive dimensions at most 100.
You may rotate each cuboid; a top cuboid must have all three oriented dimensions no greater than the one below it.
Choose any subset and maximize the sum of oriented heights.
hints: Sort each cuboid’s three dimensions so its largest dimension is the chosen height.
Sort the normalized cuboids and run a three-dimensional longest increasing subsequence.
For each bottom cuboid, extend every earlier cuboid whose three dimensions fit componentwise.
Any feasible orientation can be normalized without reducing height, and the sorted order provides a topological order for every componentwise stack relation.
editorial: Any feasible orientation can be normalized without reducing height, and the sorted order provides a topological order for every componentwise stack relation.

tests.explanation: After canonical rotations, all three cuboids stack with heights 45, 50, and 95 for total 190.
The cuboids cannot stack compatibly, so rotate the second cuboid to height 76 and use it alone.
